subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Caramelisation differs from the Maillard reaction because it involves:
options: A reaction of proteins with sugars
questions.explain: Caramelisation is the browning of sugar alone when heated, without amino acids.

questions.q: The Maillard reaction responsible for the brown crust on roast meat is a reaction between:
questions.explain: The Maillard reaction is non-enzymic browning between amino acids and reducing sugars on heating.

questions.q: The browning of a cut apple left exposed to air is caused by:
questions.explain: Enzymes (polyphenol oxidases) react with oxygen on cut surfaces, producing brown pigments.

questions.q: Which factor would increase an adult's basal metabolic rate?
options: A greater proportion of lean muscle mass
questions.explain: Lean muscle is metabolically active, so a higher muscle mass raises BMR.

questions.q: Which mineral is most associated with the prevention of iron-deficiency anaemia?
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; a deficiency causes anaemia.

questions.q: Salmonella food poisoning is most commonly associated with:
options: Raw or undercooked poultry and eggs
questions.explain: Salmonella is frequently linked to raw or undercooked poultry, eggs and their products.

questions.q: Osteoporosis is most directly linked to a long-term deficiency of:
questions.explain: Inadequate calcium and vitamin D reduce bone mineral density, leading to brittle bones.

questions.q: Lactose intolerance occurs because the person:
options: Lacks sufficient lactase enzyme to digest milk sugar
questions.explain: Without enough lactase, lactose is not digested, causing bloating and discomfort.

questions.q: 'Food security' is best defined as:
options: Selling food at a high price
All people having reliable access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food
questions.explain: Food security means everyone has consistent access to enough safe, nutritious food for a healthy life.

questions.q: Bacterial spores, such as those of Clostridium and Bacillus, are a hazard because they:
options: Can survive normal cooking temperatures and germinate later
questions.explain: Heat-resistant spores can survive cooking and germinate into active bacteria if food is mishandled.

questions.q: Lecithin in egg yolk acts as an emulsifier in mayonnaise because it:
options: Raises the pH of the mixture
Thickens the mixture by absorbing water
Coagulates the oil into solid particles
Has one part attracted to oil and one part attracted to water
questions.explain: An emulsifier has hydrophilic and hydrophobic ends, holding oil and water together as a stable emulsion.

questions.q: Vitamin C is described as enhancing iron absorption because it:
options: Binds iron so it cannot be absorbed
Converts non-haem iron into the more readily absorbed ferrous form
questions.explain: Vitamin C reduces non-haem iron to the ferrous form, which is absorbed more easily.

questions.q: Which provides the most kilojoules of energy per gram?
questions.explain: Fat provides about 37 kJ per gram, more than double that of carbohydrate or protein.

questions.q: Which is a sensory factor affecting food choice?
options: The aroma, taste and texture of a dish
questions.explain: Sensory factors include appearance, aroma, flavour, texture and sound, which influence appeal.

questions.q: In HACCP, a 'critical control point' is a step at which:
options: Control is essential to prevent or eliminate a hazard
questions.explain: A critical control point is a stage where control is essential to remove or reduce a hazard to a safe level.

questions.q: If energy intake consistently exceeds energy expenditure, the most likely outcome is:
questions.explain: A positive energy balance stores surplus energy as body fat, causing weight gain.

questions.q: On a food label, the 14 major allergens (such as nuts and milk) must be:
options: Emphasised, for example in bold, within the ingredients list
questions.explain: Law requires the 14 named allergens to be emphasised in the ingredients list so consumers can identify them.

questions.q: Mould growth on cheese such as blue cheese is an example of:
options: A harmful pathogen always causing illness
questions.explain: Certain moulds are cultivated deliberately to ripen and flavour foods like blue cheese.

questions.q: Which type of fatty acid contains no carbon-to-carbon double bonds?
questions.explain: Saturated fatty acids have all carbon bonds filled with hydrogen and no double bonds.

questions.q: A food described as containing high biological value (HBV) protein is one that:
options: Contains no amino acids at all
Contains all the essential amino acids
questions.explain: HBV proteins supply all the indispensable (essential) amino acids the body cannot synthesise.

questions.q: A complete protein from a single plant source that supplies all essential amino acids is:
questions.explain: Soya is unusual among plant foods in supplying all the essential amino acids.

questions.q: Basal metabolic rate (BMR) is defined as the energy needed to:
options: Maintain essential body functions at complete rest
questions.explain: BMR is the energy required to sustain basic functions such as respiration and circulation at rest.

questions.q: Adding lemon juice to cut fruit slows enzymic browning because:
options: The acidity inhibits the enzyme activity
questions.explain: The low pH of lemon juice denatures the browning enzymes, slowing the reaction.

questions.q: In bread-making, the biological raising of the dough is produced by:
options: Yeast fermenting sugars to release carbon dioxide
questions.explain: Yeast ferments sugars, producing carbon dioxide that makes bread dough rise.

questions.q: Cross-contamination in a kitchen is best prevented by:
options: Defrosting meat on a worktop overnight
Using the same knife for raw and cooked items
Using separate colour-coded boards for raw and cooked foods
Storing raw meat above ready-to-eat food
questions.explain: Separating raw and cooked foods, e.g. with colour-coded boards, prevents bacteria transferring between them.

questions.q: A person with coeliac disease must avoid:
options: Gluten found in wheat, barley and rye
questions.explain: Coeliac disease is an immune reaction to gluten, so wheat, barley and rye must be avoided.

questions.q: Combining beans on toast to obtain a full set of essential amino acids is an example of:
questions.explain: Protein complementation combines two LBV foods whose limiting amino acids differ to give the full set.

questions.q: Trans fatty acids in the diet are of particular concern because they:
options: Raise LDL and lower HDL cholesterol
Have no effect on blood cholesterol
Lower LDL and raise HDL cholesterol
questions.explain: Trans fats raise harmful LDL while lowering protective HDL cholesterol, increasing CHD risk.

questions.q: Salting and sugaring preserve foods primarily by:
options: Reducing the water activity available to micro-organisms
questions.explain: High salt or sugar concentrations draw water out by osmosis, lowering aw and inhibiting microbes.

questions.q: Which bonds link amino acids together within the primary structure of a protein?
questions.explain: Amino acids are joined by peptide bonds formed in a condensation reaction during protein synthesis.
